citation: Estrada-Belli, Francisco. 2011. The First Maya Civilization: Ritual and Power Before the Classic Period. London; New York: Routledge. Hardback ISBN 978-0-415-42993-1; paperback ISBN 978-0-415-42994-8; eBook ISBN 978-0-203-83913-3. DOI: https://doi.org/10.4324/9780203839133.
notes: Secondary monograph focused on Preclassic Maya ritual and power (Holmul Project region). Routledge description (accessed 2026-10-11): when Maya kings of Tikal dedicated their first carved monuments in the 3rd century A.D., inaugurating the Classic period that lasted for six centuries, Maya civilization was already nearly a millennium old; first cities such as Nakbe and El Mirador had some of the largest temples ever raised in Prehispanic America; Cival shows even earlier evidence of complex rituals; challenges older models of a simple Preclassic village age merely responding to highland stimuli. TOC covers Preclassic trajectories, states before the Classic, sacred ground, Preclassic art metanarratives, and the Preclassic-to-Classic transition.
